track.title: Original Spore asset schemas, serialization boundaries, ownership, and persistence archaeology
track.array_policy: All arrays are in authored deterministic order. No unordered-set output, random values, timestamps, wall-clock values, or runtime-generated identifiers are included.

included: DBPF record identity and record-byte extraction boundary
Property, PropertyList, DirectPropertyList, and typed value codec helpers
ClassSerializer, Attribute, and simulator serialization interfaces
CellSerializer metadata and cCellDataReference runtime resolution
Direct Cell resource records and their fixed/variable schemas
Runtime ownership, lazy loading, release, teardown, and transient-versus-persistent fields
Saved-game header, GameLoadParameters, cGamePersistenceManager, and unknown save/load framing
Current OpenSpore source and test correspondence
excluded: proprietary asset bytes, models, textures, sounds, scripts, and source copying
original-process save/load execution or runtime tracing
Ghidra mutation, re-analysis, saves, renames, and type changes
claims requiring a payload, checksum, encryption, or slot/profile trace not present in the evidence
scope.interpretation_rule: A direct Cell record layout is a content-record schema; it is not evidence that the record uses a CellSerializer envelope or that it is a player/profile save record.

evidence_base.claim: The research target is SporeApp.exe 3.1.0.22, x86:LE:32, image base 0x00400000, with the recorded SHA-256.

evidence_base.query: Read-only SporeApp.exe function, decompilation, structure, and xref queries
evidence_base.claim: Static bodies and layouts were used to establish bounded call shape and ownership behavior; no Ghidra write or save was performed.
SDK names, sizes, field offsets, enum values, and interface declarations are static evidence, not proof of undocumented behavior.
The PropertyList read/write bodies expose count/property dispatch and stream boundaries; exact value bytes remain unresolved.
The current clean-room decoders and committed tests recover direct Cell record layouts, fixed sizes, count spans, references, and domain constraints.
The original Cell data-reference path caches by instance and serializer, increments ownership, loads resources lazily, and releases/clears the cache.
The saved-game header, load parameters, persistence manager, ClassSerializer, and Cell serializable-data layouts are statically known at bounded field-level only.
An earlier campaign described a CellSerializer name/ID envelope, but the later direct-layout decoders and tests reject that model for the recovered Cell records.
OpenSpore provides identity-to-record-byte access over one borrowed DBPF package or a memory stub; it does not claim original multi-package persistence.
OpenSpore models Cell GFX world tokens, named layers, preloaded record keys, and display state as current clean-room runtime state, not original serialized bytes.
The committed runtime campaign is negative for reaching Cell Stage under the tested conditions; no original save/load trace is available.

asset_types.name: PROP
asset_types.identity: DBPF type/group/instance record containing PropertyList data.
asset_types.claim: The PROP TypeID is known, but the exact PROP record envelope, property ordering, parent encoding, and round-trip framing are not fully recovered.

asset_types.name: world_object_or_model_part
asset_types.layout: Lowercase part-name identity strings plus structural vector data; not a CellSerializer name/ID envelope.
asset_types.claim: The record is a distinct model/scene-part family, not a recovered CellSerializer envelope and not a Cell scene-placement record.

asset_types.name: cCellGlobalsResource
asset_types.layout: Direct field-by-field fixed record; every byte is accounted for by the current decoder.
asset_types.claim: This is stage-wide Cell tuning/content data, not cCellSerializableData and not player/profile save state.

asset_types.name: cCellEffectMapResource
asset_types.claim: The pointer slot is a serialized dead/preserved value and is not dereferenced by the current decoder.

asset_types.name: cCellStructureResource
asset_types.claim: The record is direct structure/effect content and carries references to other Cell resources by instance-like values.

asset_types.name: cCellBackgroundMapResource
asset_types.claim: The record supplies a background-color ramp keyed by a geometric scale ladder; the current sampler is a host-side interpretation.

asset_types.name: cCellPowersResource
asset_types.layout: int32 teleportCost followed by float32 teleportRange.
asset_types.claim: This is a fixed-size content record, not a serializer envelope or save-state object.

asset_types.name: cCellLookTableResource
asset_types.claim: Look-table rows are direct type/value records; the pointer slot is retained as a dead serialized value.

asset_types.name: cCellWorldResource
asset_types.layout: 16-byte header plus numPopulate * 12-byte level entries plus numAdvect * 24-byte advect entries.
asset_types.claim: The world record is direct count-and-array content; it is not a saved live cCellGame state object.

asset_types.name: cCellLootTableResource
asset_types.claim: Loot rows contain Cell/table references and reward tuning; the current decoder validates reference domains but does not execute loot.

asset_types.name: cCellPopulateResource
asset_types.claim: Populate records carry spawn/distribution content and references to Cell records; they do not store per-entity x/y placement in the recovered layout.

asset_types.name: cCellLookAlgorithmResource
asset_types.claim: Algorithm rows reference look-table records by instance-like values; the current decoder validates those references.

asset_types.name: cCellCellResource
asset_types.layout: Direct fixed field-by-field record containing a wide name, identity, AI blocks, behavior, and references.
asset_types.claim: The record is direct fixed-layout Cell content, not a CellSerializer name/ID envelope and not live cell state.

asset_types.name: cCellRandomCreatureResource
asset_types.claim: The record is direct spawnable-creature tuning/content and is not a runtime entity pool serialization.

schemas.claim: ResourceKey is the stable record identity used across Cell, empire, planet, mission, and property references.
The SDK supplies the union-plus-flags/type shape, but the imported Ghidra structure is only 4 bytes; the authoritative runtime layout and value encoding are not resolved.

wire_shape.normal_path: A count followed by property entries, each containing a uint32 property ID and a typed Property value.
wire_shape.entry_size_claim: 24 bytes per entry is a decompilation-derived layout clue, not a complete value encoding proof.
wire_shape.negative_count_branch: A negative-count branch reads additional words and resolves a parent; the exact branch semantics are unresolved.

schemas.claim: PropertyList has an explicit local map, parent lookup chain, operation counter, and stream Read/Write boundary; only the ID/value dispatch shape is known.
DirectPropertyList adds fast-access runtime state and a temporary Property; these fields are not evidence of a separate file format.
ClassSerializer is an object/attribute dispatch surface with binary and text callback slots, but the concrete wire format and pointer-table encoding are unknown.
Attribute exposes offset, binary read/write, and text read/write callbacks, but concrete class IDs and callback behavior are unresolved.
CellSerializerField is a metadata descriptor with name, ID, offsets, and callbacks; its field IDs and generic field envelope are not recovered.
CellSerializer metadata exists, but the recovered direct Cell records do not demonstrate a name/ID envelope around their fields.
cCellResource couples a resource byte buffer and serializer descriptor with an identity key; the direct Cell record decoders consume the buffer according to each record's own layout.
The reference object is a lazy runtime handle keyed by instance and serializer; its resource pointer and counter are ownership/runtime fields, not necessarily file fields.
This is a Cell runtime serializable-data layout candidate held by cCellGame at offset 0x5190; exact fields written on save, reset semantics, and cross-stage handoff are unknown.
The header declares major/minor versions, object counts, timestamp, mode, snapshot state, and current planet key, but its serialized placement and migration behavior are unknown.

schemas.size_confidence: MEDIUM; SDK size is marked uncertain
schemas.claim: GameLoadParameters is a declared load context containing game/star names, creature and planet references, difficulty, and mode; field consumption is unresolved.
The manager is a singleton/service with a LoadGame vtable entry, mode fields, and unresolved state; no concrete save/load body is recovered.

relationships.statement: A DBPF record is identified by type, group, and instance and yields a payload byte range; the current OpenSpore seam stops at bytes.
GetProperty searches the local sorted property map and falls back to the parent PropertyList; SetProperty mutates the local map and increments the operation counter.
PropertyList Write emits a count and then property ID/value entries through stream and value-dispatch helpers; the exact byte representation remains unresolved.
ClassSerializer owns 128 attribute slots and Attribute exposes binary/text read and write callbacks plus offset metadata.
CellSerializer points to field descriptors carrying names, IDs, sizes, offsets, and read/write callbacks.
The reference cache is keyed by instance and serializer, increments a counter, resolves a resource on demand, and releases it when the counter reaches zero or during teardown.
Direct Cell records provide content and references that can feed runtime construction, but exact selection, placement, AI activation, and spawn execution are not fully recovered.
The SDK places game/star/creature/difficulty/mode context in GameLoadParameters, and the persistence manager exposes LoadGame, but the field-consumption call path is not observed.
The header's object-count map, mode, snapshot flag, and current planet key plausibly describe saved simulator state and restoration context; no body confirms order.
cCellGame holds an intrusive pointer to cCellSerializableData at offset 0x5190; this establishes ownership, not a complete save schema.
The current provider fetches record bytes by identity; current typed Cell decoders then interpret those bytes. This is a modern content seam, not an original serializer.

steps: Select a record by ResourceKey {typeID, groupID, instanceID}.
Resolve the package index and record extent.
Expose the record bytes to a consumer.
For QFS-compressed records, decompress only when the outer container indicates QFS.
lifecycle.transient_persistent: Package index and provider lifetime are runtime state; the returned record bytes are content input and are not automatically save-state data.

steps: Match the record TypeID to a direct Cell schema.
Read fixed fields or count-prefixed rows in little-endian order.
Validate exact size, count span, pointer-slot preservation, field domains, and resource references.
Expose a typed current-source value object.
lifecycle.transient_persistent: Parsed values and vectors are host runtime projections; the original record bytes are the persisted content artifact.

steps: SetProperty inserts or updates a local property by uint32 ID.
GetProperty searches local storage and then the parent list.
DirectPropertyList uses fast-access runtime slots and a temporary Property.
The operation counter records mutations but does not imply persistence.
lifecycle.transient_persistent: Parent, fast-access values, temporary Property, and operation counter are runtime fields; only the actual stream entries are candidates for persistence.

steps: Create or retrieve a cCellDataReference by instance ID and CellSerializer pointer.
Increment the reference counter.
Resolve the cCellResource and load its bytes when absent.
Dispatch the resource serializer/record resolver on demand.
lifecycle.transient_persistent: mInstanceID is a record identity; mpSerializer, mpResource, and mCounter are runtime linkage/ownership state and are not proven serialized fields.

steps: Cell mode initializes a cCellGame singleton.
The stage holds content/runtime pools, world references, and cCellSerializableData.
The exact order of content reference resolution, pool creation, and display activation is not fully recovered.
lifecycle.transient_persistent: Live pools, render worlds, query pools, and display state are transient; cCellSerializableData is a persistence candidate only, not a proven file schema.

steps: CellGame updates the live stage and gameplay state.
Current OpenSpore has an in-process CellSim update loop, but this is not an original serialization event.
lifecycle.transient_persistent: Runtime entity, camera, frame, and query state is transient unless a separate original save path proves otherwise.

lifecycle.system: Cell resource release and mode teardown
steps: Release the cCellDataReference counter.
Clear loaded resources and tear down the cache when ownership ends.
The original cCellGame OnExit/Dispose path restores display/global side effects and releases stage state.
lifecycle.transient_persistent: Resource cache pointers, pools, worlds, and display handles are transient; no automatic save is established by teardown.

steps: A persistence manager singleton is available.
A saved-game header and serializable object contracts are declared.
The actual writer, record ordering, transaction, checksum/encryption, and mode trigger are not recovered.
lifecycle.transient_persistent: Only fields actually emitted by the missing writer can be classified as persistent; candidate object layouts must not be treated as wire format.

steps: LoadGame is present in the persistence-manager vtable.
GameLoadParameters supplies game/star/creature/difficulty/mode context.
The concrete deserialization and pointer remapping path is not recovered.
lifecycle.transient_persistent: Load context and reconstructed object references are runtime state after loading; exact archive framing is unknown.

contradictions.statement: The SDK describes a 20-byte Property with a value union and flags/type, while the imported Ghidra structure is 4 bytes with flags/type only.
contradictions.resolution: Do not choose either layout as authoritative without a runtime allocation/size proof.

contradictions.statement: Historical documentation described recovered Cell records as a CellSerializer name/ID envelope; later direct decoders and tests show fixed/count-prefixed records without that envelope.
contradictions.resolution: Use direct TypeID-specific Cell schemas for the recovered records and keep generic CellSerializer wire behavior UNKNOWN.

contradictions.statement: The SDK maps ClassSerializer Write/Read to semantic names at 0x006928C0 and 0x00693DE0, while the current live Ghidra function inventory resolves nearby addresses to unnamed bodies whose behavior does not establish the serializer implementation.
contradictions.resolution: Keep the SDK declarations as architecture evidence and do not use the nearby live bodies as semantic proof.

contradictions.topic: Dead pointer slots versus runtime pointers
contradictions.statement: Direct Cell records preserve pointer-shaped serialized values without dereferencing them, while cCellDataReference and cCellResource have real runtime pointer fields used for lazy resolution.
contradictions.resolution: Classify record pointer slots as preserved content bytes and runtime pointer fields as ownership/linkage state; do not serialize host addresses.

contradictions.statement: The recovered direct Cell TypeIDs describe content assets, while cCellGame owns live pools and a cCellSerializableData candidate for runtime state.
contradictions.resolution: Keep content decoding, live state, and save-state reconstruction as separate reconstruction packages.
